unit.title: Perform manual metal arc welding process to AWS specification (Low carbon steel pipe)

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A carbon steel pipe is ordered as "100 mm (4 inch) schedule 40". What does "schedule 40" tell the welder?
options: The length of each pipe, in feet
The highest working pressure, in bar
Its wall thickness
Its carbon content, in hundredths of a per cent

questions.stem: Why must the welder know the wall thickness of a carbon steel pipe before welding it to a WPS?
options: The WPS is qualified only for a range of wall thicknesses
A thick wall always needs a stainless steel electrode
The wall thickness decides the colour of the primer
A thin wall can only be welded in the flat position

questions.stem: A piping job is to be welded to the AWS code the Centre uses. Which document tells the welder the root gap, electrodes and passes for each joint?
options: The steel maker's mill certificate
The supplier's delivery note
The client's purchase order
The WPS

questions.stem: A pipe test is welded with the pipe standing upright, so the joint runs round it horizontally. What is the AWS position?
options: 1G
2G
5G
6G

questions.stem: Why is a pipe welded in the 1G position rolled as the weld is made?
options: So the root can be welded from inside the pipe
So the pool stays near the top, in the flat
So the pipe cools evenly and needs no inspection
So the welder need not clean between passes

questions.stem: What extra feature does a 6GR pipe test have, compared with a plain 6G test?
options: A backing ring fitted inside the root
A branch pipe welded on the side
The pipe is rolled while it is welded
A ring near the joint that restricts access

questions.stem: Pipe is stored on a rack outside the shop in Old Harbour. What must be done before one length is rolled off the rack?
options: Chock the other pipes so they cannot roll
Wet the pipes so they are cool to handle
Paint the ends so the welder can see them
Stand on the other pipes to hold them steady

questions.stem: A pipe joint must be welded in an open trench on a site. What must be in place before the welder goes in?
options: A long cable, so the machine can stay far away
Only a hard hat, since the trench is in open air
Safe trench sides and a safe way in and out
A pump to flood the trench as a fire guard

questions.stem: Why must a pipe that has carried fuel or oil never be cut or welded until a competent person has declared it clean and safe?
options: Oil makes the finished welds look dirty
The oil makes the pipe too heavy to lift
The oil will rust the inside of the pipe
Left-over vapour can explode when heated

questions.stem: While grinding a pipe bevel, a welder is sending sparks towards stacked cardboard boxes. What should the team leader do?
options: Let him finish, then sweep up afterwards
Stop the work and move or screen the boxes
Wet the welder's clothes so sparks cannot burn
Tell him to grind faster to finish sooner

questions.stem: A pipe bevel has been ground with a root face that is far too thick for the WPS. What is the likely result?
options: Too much penetration, with drips inside the bore
Porosity in the cap pass only
Lack of penetration at the root
Undercut along the outside toes of the cap

questions.stem: Which tool is best for checking the bevel angle on a pipe end?
options: A bevel protractor or pipe bevel gauge
A fillet weld gauge
A tape measure
A spirit level

questions.stem: Pipe ends have been cut and bevelled with an oxy-fuel torch. What must be done before fit-up?
options: Grind off the oxide and slag to bright metal
Paint the bevels to stop them rusting
Leave the scale on, as it helps the arc start
Wet the bevels so they cool quickly

questions.stem: Why does a WPS for an open-root pipe joint set both the root gap and the root face?
options: So the pipe looks neat before it is welded
So any electrode size can be used for the root
Together they control how the root penetrates
So that no tack welds are needed on the joint

questions.stem: A fitter uses the bare end of an electrode of the right size as a spacer to set the root gap. What must he check after tacking?
options: That the spacer is left in the gap for welding
That the gap is still even all round
That the pipe has cooled to room temperature
That the tacks have been painted over

questions.stem: On a 5G pipe joint welded uphill, why do many welders avoid placing a tack at the very bottom (6 o'clock)?
options: A tack there would be too hard to see
Tacks at the bottom always crack open
The code does not allow any low tacks
The root starts there, so a tack is in the way

questions.stem: Two pipe ends are slightly out of round, so the inside walls do not line up at one side. What is the best way to reduce this?
options: Fill the step with extra weld in the cap
Weld it as it is, as the step does not matter
Turn one pipe to find the best match, or use a clamp
Open the root gap wider at that side only

questions.stem: A weld neck flange is to be welded onto a horizontal pipe. How are the bolt holes usually lined up?
options: One hole on the top of the vertical centre line
Any way, as the holes can be redrilled later
One hole at the very bottom, on the centre line
Two holes straddling the vertical centre line

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a slip-on flange and a weld neck flange?
options: Slip-on: fillet welded; weld neck: butt welded
Slip-on: cast iron; weld neck: forged steel
Slip-on: bolted only; weld neck: glued on
Slip-on: for water only; weld neck: for air only

questions.stem: A long-radius 90° elbow has a centre-line radius of about 1.5 times its nominal size. About what is that radius for a 100 mm (4 inch) elbow?
options: About 100 mm
About 150 mm
About 200 mm
About 50 mm

questions.stem: Why is an E6010 cellulosic electrode often chosen for the open root on carbon steel pipe?
options: It needs no cleaning at all between passes
Its forceful arc digs in for a sound root
It is a low-hydrogen electrode for thick walls
It runs only on AC, from any welding machine

questions.stem: Why must E6010 electrodes NOT be baked in a hot oven the way E7018 electrodes are?
options: The coating needs some moisture to work properly
The electrodes would melt inside the oven
Baking makes them too strong for carbon steel
They would catch fire at once in any oven

questions.stem: A WPS calls for E7018 fill and cap passes after an E6010 root. What is the main reason for the change of electrode?
options: E7018 gives deeper penetration than E6010
E7018 is always cheaper than E6010
E7018 never needs to be kept in an oven
E7018 gives tough, low-hydrogen weld metal

questions.stem: When running an E6010 root on pipe, the welder uses a "whip and pause" motion. Why?
options: To stop the electrode sticking to the pipe
To lay a wide, flat cap in a single pass
To control the heat and the size of the keyhole
To blow the slag out through the root gap

questions.stem: What is the "keyhole" in an open-root pipe weld?
options: A hole drilled to let gas out of the pipe
A slot cut in the flange for a bolt
A fault caused by too low a current
The small hole at the front of the pool

questions.stem: During an open root, the keyhole keeps getting bigger. What should the welder do?
options: Slow down and hold the arc longer in the hole
Turn the current up so the hole fills faster
Speed up, or shorten the arc's time in the pool
Change at once to a larger electrode

questions.stem: On a pipe root, what are "wagon tracks"?
options: Scratches left on the pipe by the rollers
Lines of slag trapped along both toes
Marks left on the pipe by the work clamp
Ridges on the outside of a weaved cap

questions.stem: How does a hot pass, run soon after the root, deal with wagon tracks?
options: Its heat melts out the slag and fuses the toes
It cools the root so the slag falls out by itself
It covers the slag over so that it cannot be seen
It hardens the slag so it no longer counts as a fault

questions.stem: On a 5G joint welded uphill, why is each pass split into two halves, each starting near the bottom?
options: So both halves run uphill and meet at the top
So two welders can never work on one joint
So the root can be left half done overnight
So the start of the pass is hidden at the top

questions.stem: On a 2G pipe joint, the cap sags along its top edge. Which change helps most?
options: One wide weave right across the joint
Small stringers stacked from the bottom, angled up
A longer arc and a higher current
Starting the cap with the top bead first

questions.stem: Why is a power wire brush or grinder used between passes on pipe, and not only a chipping hammer?
options: It makes the weld cool down faster
It hardens the surface of each pass
It clears slag from the toes and ripples
It gives the shine that inspectors want

questions.stem: Inside a pipe root, drops of metal hang down into the bore ("icicles"). What is the likely cause?
options: Too little current for the root pass
A root gap that was set too small
A root face that was ground too thick
Too much heat, or too wide a gap, at that spot

questions.stem: A pipe weld looks perfect on the outside. Why may the inspector still call for radiography?
options: Radiography makes the weld itself stronger
The cap colour tells nothing about the steel
Faults such as lack of root fusion are hidden inside
The code needs every weld painted before use

questions.stem: On a pipe test with a thick wall, side bends are used in place of face and root bends. Why?
options: A side bend tests the whole wall across the weld
Side bends need no cutting, so they are cheaper
Face bends cannot be made on carbon steel
Side bends test only the cap, which is thickest

questions.stem: A face bend strip from a pipe test opens a crack bigger than the code allows. What does this mean?
options: The test passes if the other strips are good
The test fails; a retest follows the code's rules
The crack is ground out and the strip bent again
Only the cap of the coupon is welded again

questions.stem: Who should carry out radiography (X-ray or gamma ray testing) of pipe welds?
options: Any welder who owns a camera
Trainees, after one short lesson
The welder who made the weld
Licensed, trained people, with the area cleared

questions.stem: Kemar passes an AWS test on 6G carbon steel pipe. Why can he not weld any pipe size or wall thickness he likes?
options: Pipe welds never need a qualified welder
His test covers only the exact pipe he welded
Only plate tests can cover other pipe sizes
The code limits the sizes and walls his test covers

questions.stem: Generally, a pipe groove test also qualifies a welder for plate, but a plate test does not qualify small-bore pipe. Why?
options: Plate is made from a different kind of steel
On pipe, the position keeps changing round the joint
Pipe is always welded with smaller electrodes
Plate test pieces are never bent or X-rayed

questions.stem: Before a pipe test starts, the assessor stamps or marks the test coupon. Why?
options: So the coupon cannot be swapped, and results are traced
So the coupon is easier to hold in the vice
So the welder knows where to start the root
So the bend tester can find the weld

questions.stem: Pipe work is often drawn as an isometric. What does this kind of drawing show?
options: Only the bolt sizes for the flanges
The inside of the pipe cut in half
The run in 3-D, with lengths, fittings and welds
The welder's qualification record

questions.stem: A 114.3 mm OD pipe joint needs 5 passes. Each pass is about 360 mm long. About how much weld is laid in total?
options: About 0.7 m
About 1.8 m
About 3.6 m
About 5.0 m

questions.stem: A pipe spool has 8 butt welds. Each takes 50 minutes of welding plus 25 minutes for fit-up and cleaning. How many hours is that in total?
options: 6.7 hours
8 hours
10 hours
12 hours

questions.stem: You lead a pipe crew on a hotel water line in Ocho Rios. A welder wants to skip the hot pass to save time. What should you do?
options: Agree, as the cap will cover any slag
Agree, if he uses a bigger electrode
Let the client decide on the day
Refuse: the WPS passes must be followed

questions.stem: Pipe welding is done in a breezy spot near the sea. Why is a wind screen put up round the joint?
options: Wind blows away the arc shield, causing porosity
Wind makes the electrodes melt much faster
Wind cools the welder down too much
Wind changes the machine's current setting

questions.stem: Before a welded carbon steel pipe spool is handed over, what should be done to its inside?
options: Leave the slag, as water flow will wash it out
Coat the inside with an oil-based paint
Clear out slag and debris, and check the bore
Fill it with sand to protect it on the way

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the AWS position code for a pipe test welded with the pipe axis at 45° and a restriction ring fitted?
What do the letters NPS stand for when pipe is ordered?
A pipe has an outside diameter of 60.3 mm and a wall 3.9 mm thick. What is its inside diameter, in mm?
Which AWS electrode class, starting with E60, has a cellulose coating and is run on DCEP for open roots?
What is the name of the flange with a long tapered hub that is butt welded to the pipe?
What is the AWS term for the distance the two pipe ends are set apart at the root before tacking?
What is the name of the test that uses X-rays or gamma rays to look inside a pipe weld?
Name the bend test strip, cut across the weld, that is used instead of face and root bends on thick-wall pipe.
A WPS gives a root face of 1.6 mm. The fitter measures 2.4 mm. By how many millimetres is it too thick?
What is the name of the passes, laid between the hot pass and the cap, that build up the groove?
A crew completes 4 pipe joints a day. How many full working days are needed for a line with 26 joints?
What is the name of the fitting that turns a pipe run through 90°?
What is the name of the thin grinding disc, able to fit in the root gap, used to open up or clean a tight root?
A 6 m pipe is cut into spool pieces 1.45 m long, allowing 5 mm for each cut. How many full pieces can be cut?
What is the AWS position code for a pipe butt weld made with the pipe rolled and welded on top?

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare, fit up and tack two carbon steel pipe ends for an open-root butt joint to a WPS, including the checks you would make.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the WPS for the bevel angle, root face, root gap and electrodes, and confirm the pipe size and wall from the markings. I cut the ends square and bevel them by machine or torch, then grind the bevels and 25 mm inside and out to bright metal. I check the bevel angle with a gauge and grind the root face to the size given. I set the pipes on stands or rollers in line, using a clamp or straight edge. I set the root gap with a spacer of the right size and check it is even all round. I check that the inside walls line up and turn a pipe if they do not. I tack in three or four places, avoiding the spot where the root will start, and feather the ends of each tack. I then check the gap and alignment again before welding.
markingPoints: Reads the WPS and confirms pipe size and wall
Square cut, bevel and clean to bright metal
Checks bevel angle and root face against the WPS
Sets an even root gap and lines up the inside walls
Tacks in the right places, feathers them and re-checks

essays.stem: Explain how an open root is run with E6010 on carbon steel pipe, including the keyhole, the motion used and how the welder controls penetration.
essays.modelAnswer: The E6010 root is run on DCEP with the current from the WPS. The welder strikes on the bevel or a tack and pushes the arc into the gap until a small keyhole opens at the front of the pool. The keyhole shows that both root faces are melting through. The welder then uses a whip and pause motion: the arc is flicked forward a little to let the pool freeze, then brought back to the pool and held for a moment to fill it. If the keyhole grows too big, the welder speeds up or shortens the pause; if it closes, he slows down or pushes in more. The electrode angle and a tight arc keep the root bead even inside. Stops are made at a tack or ground to a taper, and the root is cleaned and checked before the hot pass.
markingPoints: DCEP and WPS current; keyhole shows root melting through
Whip and pause motion explained
Controls keyhole size by speed and pause time
Tight arc and correct angle for an even inside bead
Clean stops and tie-ins; root cleaned and checked

essays.stem: Compare welding a carbon steel pipe joint in the 2G and the 6G positions. Cover the electrode angles, the bead pattern and the defects to watch for.
essays.modelAnswer: In 2G the pipe stands upright and the weld runs round it horizontally. The welder stays at much the same angle all the way round, with the electrode tilted a little upward. The fill and cap are laid as small stringer beads stacked from the bottom up, each one overlapping the last. The main faults are sagging on the top edge, undercut on the upper toe and slag between beads. In 6G the pipe is fixed at 45°, so the welder passes through overhead, vertical and flat in each half. The electrode angle must change all the time to follow the joint, and the beads are usually weaved or stacked depending on the WPS. The faults to watch are lack of fusion on the upper bevel, concavity at the bottom and poor tie-ins at the top and bottom.
markingPoints: 2G: pipe upright, steady slight upward angle
2G: stacked stringers; sag and upper toe undercut
6G: 45°, all positions, constant angle change
6G: fusion on upper bevel, root concavity, tie-ins
Clear comparison of both

essays.stem: Explain the job of each pass in a carbon steel pipe weld (root, hot pass, fill and cap) and how the slag is dealt with between passes.
essays.modelAnswer: The root pass fuses the two pipe ends at the bottom of the groove and forms the inside bead. It must have full penetration with no burn-through. The hot pass follows soon after, at a higher current. It melts out any slag trapped along the edges of the root, the wagon tracks, and makes the root thicker so it does not crack or burn through on later passes. The fill passes build up the groove with sound, low-hydrogen metal, fused well into the side walls. The cap is the final pass. It fills the groove to just above the pipe surface, about 1.5 mm wide over each edge, with no undercut. Between every pass the slag is removed with a chipping hammer and a power wire brush, and any high spots are ground, so that no slag is trapped.
markingPoints: Root: fusion and penetration of the ends
Hot pass: burns out wagon tracks, strengthens root
Fill: builds up with good side wall fusion
Cap: final size, no undercut
Cleans slag fully between passes

essays.stem: Describe the common defects in carbon steel pipe roots (lack of penetration, burn-through, icicles, concavity and wagon tracks). Give a cause and a cure for each.
essays.modelAnswer: Lack of penetration is caused by too small a gap, too thick a root face or too little current. The cure is to fit up to the WPS and keep a keyhole. Burn-through is a hole caused by too much heat, a wide gap or slow travel; the cure is to speed up, shorten the pause or lower the current within the range. Icicles are drops hanging inside the bore from too much heat at one spot; the cure is steadier travel and an even gap. Concavity, or suck-back, is a hollow root on the inside, often at the bottom of a 5G or 6G joint, from too long an arc or too much heat; pushing the electrode in and keeping a tight arc helps. Wagon tracks are slag lines along the root toes; a correct hot pass and good cleaning remove them.
markingPoints: Lack of penetration: cause and cure
Burn-through: cause and cure
Icicles: cause and cure
Concavity: cause and cure
Wagon tracks: cause and cure

essays.stem: Explain how bend test strips are cut, prepared and bent from a carbon steel pipe test coupon, and how the bent strips are judged.
essays.modelAnswer: After the coupon passes a visual check, strips are cut across the weld from the places the code sets out, so that each part of the joint is tested, such as the top, bottom and sides of a fixed pipe. The cut is made with a saw or by machine, not by torch near the weld. The cap and root are ground or machined flush with the pipe, along the length of the strip, and the edges are rounded slightly so cracks do not start from saw marks. For a thinner wall, face and root bends are used; for a thick wall, side bends. Each strip is bent in a guided bend jig round a former of the size the code gives, with the face, root or side on the outside. The strips are then checked. Open cracks or defects over the size the code allows mean a fail.
markingPoints: Strips cut from set places after visual check
Cut cold; cap and root dressed flush; edges rounded
Face and root bends for thin wall, side bends for thick wall
Bent in a guided jig round the set former
Judged against the code's crack limits

essays.stem: Describe how you would weld a weld neck flange onto a carbon steel pipe so that the flange face is square and the bolt holes line up.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the flange's size and pressure class against the drawing and clean the bevels. I set the pipe level on stands and fit the flange with the root gap from the WPS. I line up the bolt holes so that two holes straddle the vertical centre line, checking with a level across two holes. I check that the flange face is square to the pipe with a flange square in two directions at 90°. I tack lightly at four points and check squareness and the bolt holes again. Then I weld the root and the other passes in a balanced order, for example opposite quarters, so that shrinkage does not pull the face out of square. I check the face again after the root and after the cap. I protect the machined face from spatter and arc strikes throughout.
markingPoints: Checks flange class and cleans; sets root gap
Two-holes the bolt holes, checked with a level
Checks face squareness with a flange square
Tacks and welds in a balanced order, re-checking
Protects the flange face from spatter and arc strikes

essays.stem: Describe the hazards of welding carbon steel pipe on an outdoor site, such as in a trench or near the sea, and how you would control them.
essays.modelAnswer: A trench can collapse, so it must be shored or sloped, with a safe ladder in and out, and no spoil or machines near the edge. Fumes can collect in a deep trench, so it is ventilated and the welder is checked on. Rain and wet ground raise the risk of electric shock, so the machine is kept dry, cables are checked, and work stops in rain. Wind blows away the arc shield, so screens are put up. Heavy pipe can roll or fall, so it is chocked and lifted with the right slings, and hands are kept out of pinch points. Sparks can start fires in dry grass, so the area is cleared and an extinguisher kept close. Hot pipe can burn, so it is marked. People passing by are kept away from arc flash with screens.
markingPoints: Trench collapse and access controls
Fume in trenches and ventilation
Electric shock in wet conditions
Pipe handling, rolling and pinch points
Fire, wind and public protection

essays.stem: Explain how you would use a piping isometric drawing to plan the fabrication of a carbon steel pipe spool, including cut lengths, fittings, weld numbers and order of work.
essays.modelAnswer: I first check the drawing number and revision, and read the title block for the pipe size, schedule and material. I list the fittings shown, such as elbows, tees and flanges, and check they are in stock. The isometric gives centre-to-centre lengths, so to find each cut length I take away the centre-to-end size of each fitting and allow for the root gaps. I write a cut list. I mark the weld numbers from the drawing on the spool as it is built, so each weld can be traced to its welder and inspection. I plan the order so that as many joints as possible can be rolled and welded in the flat (1G), and only the last closing joints are welded fixed. I also plan where the spool is checked for length and squareness before the final welds.
markingPoints: Checks revision, size, schedule and material
Lists fittings and works out cut lengths from centre-to-end sizes
Allows for root gaps; makes a cut list
Uses weld numbers for traceability
Plans order to roll welds where possible and check dimensions

essays.stem: As team leader of a pipe crew, explain how you would keep the quality of welds on a carbon steel pipe job, from issuing electrodes to final inspection and records.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the job starts I check that every welder is qualified for the pipe size, wall and positions, and that each has read the WPS. I make sure E7018 electrodes are kept in an oven and issued in small amounts in a heated quiver, and that E6010 electrodes are kept in their sealed tins. I check fit-ups before welding: bevel, root face, gap and alignment. I watch the root and hot pass and check the current. I make sure slag is removed between passes and that wind screens are used outside. Each weld is given its number and the welder's mark, and the details go on the weld log. I carry out visual inspection of each finished weld and send welds for radiography or other tests as the job asks. Repairs are recorded and re-checked. I report the weld count and repair rate to the supervisor.
markingPoints: Checks qualifications and WPS briefing
Controls electrode storage and issue by type
Checks fit-up and watches root and settings
Weld numbers, weld log and traceability
Inspection, testing, repairs recorded and reported

practical1.title: Open-root carbon steel pipe butt weld in the 2G position, E6010 root and E7018 fill and cap, to a WPS
practical1.brief: Your group is given a WPS for a carbon steel pipe butt joint. Each member prepares and welds one short pipe coupon (two pieces of about 100–150 mm pipe, as the assessor provides) in the 2G position (pipe upright, weld running round it). Each member bevels or checks the bevels, sets the root face and gap, tacks, then welds an E6010 root, a hot pass and E7018 fill and cap passes, cleaning between passes. Before welding, members check each other's fit-up and record the bevel angle, root face and gap on the group's weld record sheet. After welding, each member inspects another member's coupon by eye (cap height, undercut, root penetration inside) and records the result. The assessor then chooses one coupon to cut for bend tests. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the weld record sheet once for the whole group.
materials: Bevelled carbon steel pipe pieces, about 100–150 mm outside diameter, two per member
E6010 electrodes (in a sealed tin) and E7018 electrodes (from the oven, in a heated quiver)
DC welding machine for each booth
Pipe stand or positioner set for 2G, and a line-up clamp or spacer
Bevel gauge, root gap gauge, weld gauge and mirror
Grinder with grinding and thin cutting discs, wire brush, chipping hammer
WPS and blank weld record sheet (from the assessor)
photos: Fit-up of one coupon with the gauge showing the root gap
A root pass, cleaned, before the hot pass
Inside of a root, seen with a mirror or after cutting
Finished caps on every member's coupon
Bend test strips from the chosen coupon after bending
checklist: Checked bevel angle, root face and gap against the WPS and recorded them
Tacked correctly and kept the root gap even
Ran an E6010 root with an even keyhole and full penetration
Used a hot pass and cleaned slag fully between passes
Laid E7018 fill and cap passes in the 2G pattern with no sagging
Inspected another member's coupon and recorded it correctly
Kept E7018 electrodes in the quiver and worked safely throughout
safety: Weld only in booths or behind screens, with fume extraction on
Hot pipe stays on the stand or in the quench area, marked HOT
Wear a face shield over safety glasses when grinding; check the disc speed rating
Keep the machine and cables dry; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Small carbon steel pipe spool with a weld neck flange and an elbow, built from an isometric drawing
practical2.brief: As a group, build a small carbon steel pipe spool from the assessor's isometric drawing: for example, a weld neck flange, a straight pipe, a 90° long-radius elbow and a second straight pipe. First, together, read the isometric and write a cut list, working out each pipe length from the centre-to-end sizes of the fittings and the root gaps. Give each joint a weld number. Share the work: one member cuts and bevels, one fits up the flange (bolt holes two-holed and face square), one fits up the elbow, and every member welds at least one pass on a numbered joint, as the WPS gives. One member keeps the weld log (weld number, welder, passes, checks). When finished, measure the spool against the drawing and check the flange face is square. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the cut list, weld log and check sheet once for the whole group.
materials: Carbon steel pipe, about 50–100 mm nominal size, as the assessor gives
One weld neck flange and one 90° long-radius butt weld elbow to suit the pipe
E6010 and E7018 electrodes as the WPS gives
Pipe stands or rollers, line-up clamp, flange square, spirit level
Tape, bevel gauge, root gap gauge, paint marker
Isometric drawing, WPS, blank cut list, weld log and check sheet
photos: The isometric drawing and the group's worked cut list
Flange fitted up, with the level showing the two-holed bolt holes
Flange squareness being checked with the flange square
Elbow joint tacked, with the weld number marked
The finished spool with all weld numbers showing
The spool being measured against the drawing, and the completed weld log
checklist: Worked out cut lengths correctly from the isometric
Cut, bevelled and cleaned pipe ends to the WPS
Lined up flange bolt holes and checked the face square
Welded at least one pass of sound quality on a numbered joint
Filled in the weld log or check sheet accurately
Finished spool within the tolerance the assessor gives
Handled pipe safely, chocked on stands, and cleaned the work area
safety: Chock pipe on stands or rollers so it cannot roll; keep hands out of pinch points
